text:
For as long as the Golden Knights have existed, they have treated SAP Center like a rest stop. Vegas came in 16-0-3 there all time, according to Sharks Hockey Digest's Max Miller. On Friday the Sharks won 4-1, their first regulation win over Vegas in their own building, and it was not a fluke.

The first period was close, and nobody scored. Carter Hart's best moment came in the second, stopping Alexander Wennberg on a 39% chance, but Wennberg's line kept coming. At 15:51 Michael Misa, whose name has been all over Simon Edvinsson trade rumors this week, finished a wrist shot from Wennberg and Tyler Toffoli. Miller wrote that the Misa-Wennberg-Toffoli line "has dominated," and the numbers back him: San Jose won the second 1.93 to 1.08 in expected goals (the quality of chances, added up).

Adam Gaudette made it 2-0 at 5:22 of the third off a rush started by Macklin Celebrini. Jack Eichel answered on the power play at 10:35, Mitch Marner and Tomas Hertl assisting, and for a few minutes Vegas had a pulse. Zack Ostapchuk ended that at 14:04 on a 3% snap shot, the least likely goal of the night, after Barclay Goodrow started the play and Collin Graf found him with a spinning pass. Celebrini hit the empty net at 17:49.

Yaroslav Askarov was the first star and earned it: 27 saves on 28 shots, about 1.6 goals better than those shots deserved, and a team-high 0.31 wins added. Our replays of every shot gave San Jose the win 69% of the time, and the Sharks were far better at even strength, 2.66 expected goals to 0.75. Vegas did win 40 of 60 faceoffs, which makes the territorial gap even more striking. The Golden Knights were coming off a signature win in Edmonton, led by Eichel and rookie Trevor Connelly. This was the other side of the week: a young Sharks team that simply had more of the puck, and a building that finally got to celebrate against the team that had owned it.
headline: Sharks finally beat Vegas in regulation at home
